promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 3 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Two weeks off doesn't send you back to the start. On Monday you pick up one small step below your last run, then the run bits get longer. You can realistically finish on Nov 15, but running every step is a stretch.

answers.question: I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?
answers.answer:
**No, you don't have to start again.** Two weeks off costs you a little fitness, not the weeks of work before it. Your last runs felt 6/10, with no pain and a steady heart rate. So Monday starts one small step below your last run on Sat Oct 3, and you build from there.

**Finishing on Sun Nov 15 is realistic, but running every step is a stretch.** Running 5K without walking means about 40 minutes of non-stop running, and your longest run bit so far is 2 minutes. If the next three weeks go to plan, you can reach run bits of about 15 minutes. That gets you round with two or three short walk breaks.

| Week | Longest run bit | Saturday session |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 19 – 25 | 4 min | 5 x 4 min run, 1 min walk |
| Oct 26 – Nov 1 | 8 min | 3 x 8 min run, 1 min walk |
| Nov 2 – 8 | 15 min | 2 x 15 min run, 1 min walk |
| Nov 9 – 15 | race week | one short walk-run, then the race |

I'd plan the race as "run as long as you comfortably can, then walk for 1 min", and treat no walking at all as a bonus. If you get through every session and feel strong, we can cut back the walk breaks in race week.

new.analysis:
**You missed the whole week, and missed weeks are the main thing standing between you and Nov 15.** None of the three planned walk-runs from Oct 12 – 18 happened, and the week before was the same. You had good reasons, but three of the last five weeks had no running at all.

**Your fitness is in better shape than the gap suggests.** On Sep 28 and Oct 3 the walk-runs felt 6/10 with no pain. Your heart rate also dropped slightly as each session went on. The 2 min run bits were well within what you can do, so the plan lengthens them this week rather than repeating them again.

**Monday is the test, and Wednesday and Saturday only step up if it goes well.** The plan has stuck at 2 min run bits for weeks because sessions kept getting missed. With four weeks to the race it can't keep doing that. Going from 2 to 3 to 4 min run bits adds only a few minutes of running, and the walk breaks keep it gentle.

**Slowing your run bits down is the biggest change you can make.** On Oct 3 your heart rate averaged 143, and nearly all of the session was in zone 3. That's because you ran the run bits at about 7:40 per km. A slower jog is how a 4 min run bit becomes a 15 min one, and on race day steady slow running beats faster running with more walking.

**For you, this stage of training means longer run bits, not faster ones.** There are no intervals or race-pace sessions. Every run stays easy, because the goal is to keep running, not to run quickly.

**Sticking with it matters more than any single session.** If looking after your mum takes a run day, move that session to the next day and carry on. If two sessions slip in the same week, repeat this week next week rather than skipping ahead.

You restarted running in the week of Oct 19 after two weeks off. Your last run before that was a 24 min walk-run on Sat Oct 3.
